rationale: All three lenses ran with spec present. Implementation matches spec design 1-4, but two required criteria are only partially evidenced by tests: AC3 (no end-to-end test of ensure_personal_project_async with a mixed-case application) and AC2 (no view-level test that the admin user detail marks exactly one default for a real+orphan user). Dismissed 9 lens concerns as pre-existing, already guarded or out of scope (None old_email is guarded by same_project_name; soft-deleted case-variant behaviour unchanged; concurrent case-variant creation needs a DB constraint, a stated non-goal; stored-default swap needs case-variant shared projects that aget_or_create prevents; orphan always equals the email string passed at login so the tie-break holds). Deferred: repeated warning for foreign case-variants (spec says skip-and-warn, code raises ValueError, behaviour equivalent), casefold vs SQL lower for exotic Unicode, reconcile not removing pre-fix orphans on a non-case email change.

business_review.item: AC1: mixed-case email user gets exactly one personal-project membership with the real name; no orphan created
business_review.notes: _find_application is case-insensitive; membership lookup and insert use application.name; tests test_create_personal_project_does_not_add_orphan_for_mixed_case_application and test_has_personal_project_complete_matches_mixed_case_application.

business_review.item: AC2: admin user details show exactly one default project for such users
business_review.notes: Resolver tests only (test_membership_default_prefers_real_row); no test drives the admin detail/list/profile views.

business_review.item: AC3: unit tests cover mixed-case emails in ensure_personal_project_async, resolve_default_project, _unfunded_project
business_review.notes: resolve_default_project and _unfunded_project covered; ensure_personal_project_async only via a test that mocks both collaborators (activity event name).

business_review.item: AC4: existing prod orphans found, removed, count reported
business_review.notes: Overridden by the product owner: no migration, script or cleanup (spec Non-goals and Decisions).

business_review.item: AC5: budget attribution names the project actually charged
business_review.notes: Four comparison sites use same_project_name with tests; grep sweep performed in Task 4 found no other personal-project comparisons (legacy_jwt username workspace and usage_attribution.is_personal_project are unrelated).

business_review.item: Design 1: canonical project name in personal-project setup
business_review.notes: Real name used for membership, activity event and reconcile; case-only reconcile is a no-op; foreign or non-personal case variants rejected.

business_review.item: Design 2: resolve_default_project case-insensitive, prefers name differing from email, sorted tie-break
business_review.notes: same_project_name and _pick_member in security/user.py with tests.

business_review.item: Design 3: personal-project detection in budget code
business_review.notes: _unfunded_project, llm_factory (2 sites), proxy_router use the shared helper.

business_review.item: Design 4: existing orphan rows stay harmless
business_review.notes: Default resolves to the real project; orphan has no application so is not listed.

business_review.item: Tests list: includes admin detail/list/profile marking exactly one default for real+orphan user

standards_review.notes: ruff check and format pass on touched files.
No email in logs (user_id and project_type only); no new inputs or secrets.

findings.title: No end-to-end test of ensure_personal_project_async with a mixed-case application
findings.problem: AC3 names ensure_personal_project_async, but its only mixed-case test mocks both _has_personal_project_complete and _create_personal_project, so the no-duplicate-membership behaviour is never asserted through the public entry point.
findings.impact: A regression that reintroduces the lowercase aadd_project call inside the real flow would pass the unit tests.
findings.recommendation: Add tests that run ensure_personal_project_async with the real helpers: (a) mixed-case application plus the real membership already present, assert aadd_project is never called and True is returned; (b) mixed-case application with only an orphan lowercase membership, assert aadd_project is called once with the real name.

findings.title: No view-level test for exactly one default with real plus orphan memberships
findings.problem: The spec's test list and AC2 require the admin detail/list/profile to mark exactly one is_default: true on the real row for a user with both the real and the orphan membership; only resolve_membership_default is tested.
findings.impact: The user-visible symptom of the ticket (empty Default radio) is not pinned by any test at the layer where it appears.
findings.recommendation: Add a test in the user_management_service tests (detail view) with memberships [real, orphan lowercase] where the orphan has no application, asserting a single ProjectInfo with is_default True for the real project; add the list-view equivalent if the same helper is used there.
